Source   Edit  

sandbox.nim — bash tool execution with optional Docker/Wasm isolation.

Modes (SandboxMode from config/types): smNone — direct exec in paddock dir; no OS-level isolation smDocker — ephemeral container with bind-mounted paddock smWasm — wasmtime CLI executing go-busybox shell.wasm

Docker mode: docker run --rm -v {paddock}:/workspace -w /workspace {image} sh -c {cmd}

Wasm mode: wasmtime run --dir={paddock} --dir=/tmp {busybox} {applet} {args}

The binary is go-busybox (https://github.com/rcarmo/go-busybox) — a multi-call binary with 57 applets (cat, grep, sed, echo, ls, etc.). MUST be named "busybox" (no extension) so argv0 dispatches correctly. Build with: scripts/setup_shell_wasm.sh

Call sandboxLogLevel once at daemon startup to surface the active mode.

    tags: [], forbids: [].}
Returns the wasmtime invocation string for go-busybox applets. The binary must be named "busybox" so that argv0 dispatches correctly. Note: go-busybox's ash shell is stubbed under WASI, so complex shell features (pipes, redirections, shell scripts) won't work. Simple applet calls (cat, grep, sed, echo, ls, etc.) work fine. Executes cmd in the appropriate sandbox for mode. For smNone: runs directly with paddock as CWD. For smDocker: wraps cmd in an ephemeral container with paddock bind-mounted. For smWasm: runs via wasmtime + go-busybox. Pipes are composed in Nim (ShellComposer) since WASI lacks fork/exec. Falls back to direct exec if shell.wasm is missing. Source   Edit
